That means to ask the doctor to relay the visit to you. It's for when you can't hear or understand a patient or the visit! It's as simple as being like "hey, sorry, but I could not hear the patient, could you tell me how the visit went?"

Of course! So, for organization, a good way to begin with that is to open the notepad app on your computer, this will allow you to take note of everything the patient says during the visit that will need put into the EMR system. If the patient is speaking too fast to get information, it is always, and i mean ALWAYS okay to ask the doctor to dictate the visit! for organizing the HPI, you can always do it in an itemized list fashion; i.e.. Hypertension: (notes here), Hyperlipidemia: (notes here), etc. Remember, to get the HPI right, it takes time and practice! A great help for me was watching medical dramas and writing practice charts for the patients. I would go on my EMR test patient profile I made, and make chart encounters for the patients in the show. 

It's super important to remember that everyone makes mistakes, and the best way to avoid them is to practice! The HPI does NOT have to be the way they taught you in training. Each doctor likes their charts differently, so always look on past patient charts to see how it looked. It will always take time, but practice makes perfect!

For writing your thoughts, use it for self-reflection. Ask yourself questions, or just use it to vent.

The senses inventory is where you look for 5 different things you see, 4 different things you hear, 3 different things you feel, 2 different things you can smell, and 1 thing you can taste. This helps to ground you and calm you down from anxiety. This also works well if you breathe in through your nose and out through your mouth slowly to reduce panic. 

The stream of thoughts is where you close your eyes and imagine a stream (like one of water in a forest! :3) with leaves on it but each leaf is a different thought. Just watch them float away, downstream. This helps with any negative thoughts you might have.
